# Independent audit: sharp triangle cap-incidence threshold

Audited in full:
`candidate ca9f00bdb64d6d9e`.
Result: PASS, with no correction identified.

The two-strict-vertex cap has the stated strictly concave area
function in its edge-intercept parameter. Moving away from its
maximum decreases area all the way to the relevant interval
endpoint. A positive-circuit boundary would create opposite
normals, whose closed cap fractions sum to one; this is excluded
by the common strict bound below one half. Successive rotations
therefore terminate at actual vertex incidences without moving
the source or the body.

The source barycentric lower bounds are valid for corner caps
including an intercept equal to one. The refinement for a source
coordinate at least one half proves that the reduced menu has
all source coordinates below one half. This justifies both
endpoints of the interval used in the subsequent minimax step.

At a vertex boundary cut, the exact first cap fraction is
z/(x+z). The other two lower bounds are 4xz and4xy. The two
cases t<=1/2 and t>1/2 exhaust the parameter range, and their
minimax calculation gives c^2+6c-3>=0 exactly. The affine
sharpness margins vanish at the displayed source and have the
stated positive dependence; their three cap fractions are all
2sqrt(3)-3.

The conclusion excludes both a second strictly captured vertex
and a second boundary vertex when c<2sqrt(3)-3. In particular,
the exact comparison128/279<2sqrt(3)-3 validates the strict
distinct-vertex incidence premise in
`candidate 3ae81051c7da6046`
under that ordinary cap ceiling. It supplies no mixed-integer
compatibility or genuine criticality beyond its stated premises.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
